sourceIssues.printed: “dim Fil_i(ǧ), i ≥ 0” (table headers); the half-spin calculation uses maximal i with dim Fil_i nonzero.
sourceIssues.correction: Use dim gr_i^Fil(ǧ), equivalently the h-eigenvalue-i multiplicity, in the table headers and the appendix computations describing the entries. In the half-spin maximum, likewise use nonzero gr_i instead of nonzero Fil_i. The lemma itself may retain equality of genuine filtration dimensions, since finite differences give equality of all graded dimensions and cumulative sums recover the filtration dimensions.
sourceIssues.reason: Definition 2.2 explicitly specifies an increasing filtration. The F4 principal row begins 4,0,4, which cannot be dimensions of nested subspaces. Moreover an exhaustive increasing filtration on a nonzero half-spin module remains nonzero for all sufficiently large i, so its nonzero Fil_i have no maximal index. Direct root enumeration reproduces every entry of the principal F4, E8 and G2 rows as graded multiplicities, including the rank-dimensional zero weight and symmetric negative weights; their total dimensions are 52,248,14. The F4 principal filtration has dim Fil_0=28, not 4. The issue is a confusion of graded and cumulative dimensions, not evidence that these three checked rows have wrong multiplicities. Other rows have not all been recomputed.

sourceIssues.printed: ℜ(s)=ω₁+ω₂+½ω₃+½ω₄ for the B₃ orbit in F₄.
sourceIssues.correction: Delete ω₂: ℜ(s)=ω₁+½ω₃+½ω₄. In the Euclidean coordinates of (6.21), the corrected dominant representative is (5/2,1,1/2,0). This is Weyl-conjugate to (2,−1,3/2,1/2), the parameter at ν=1/2 in the B3 complementary series.
sourceIssues.reason: Using the explicit fundamental weights (6.21), the printed parameter is (4,3/2,1,1/2), with squared norm 39/2. Ciubotaru’s primary classification [Ci1], §3.2 table continued on manuscript p.14 and §5 p.37, gives B3 parameters (3/2+ν,−3/2+ν,3/2,1/2), 0≤ν<1, in the SAME coordinates (§2.6 p.10). Their squared norms are 7+2ν²<9, so the printed point is not Weyl-conjugate to any member of this complementary series. The nonzero half-integral value is ν=1/2. Its coordinate vector (2,−1,3/2,1/2) first becomes (2,3/2,1,1/2) by a signed permutation and then (5/2,1,1/2,0) by reflection in (1,−1,−1,−1). This equals ω₁+½ω₃+½ω₄. Independent enumeration gives top adjoint Frobenius weight 16 for the printed point, contradicting the p.34 bound 10. The corrected point has multiplicities n_v(10)=1,n_v(9)=0,n_v(8)=2, as needed there. The coordinate classification statement must therefore be repaired, in addition to the index repair E3; no failure of the intended global theorem is asserted.
